beats.say: This is part two of leading your first team meeting: running the room.
Open with a clear purpose, then spend most of the meeting listening.

scenes.headline: Let the team talk first.
scenes.aside: Your job is mostly to listen.

beats.say: Say why you called the meeting and what you hope to leave with. Then hand the floor over quickly.
In this first meeting, your job is mostly to listen.
Go around the room. Ask each person what they're working on,
and one thing that would make their work easier. Write it where everyone can see.

scenes.headline: Read the room as you go.

cards.title: The quiet one
cards.question: Invite them in by name, gently.

cards.title: The loud topic
cards.question: Park it, with a clear promise to come back to it.

cards.title: Fast agreement
cards.question: Ask: what would make this fail?

beats.say: As people talk, watch for three patterns.
The quiet person who hasn't spoken yet. Invite them in by name, gently.
The loudest topic that takes over. Park it, with a clear promise to return to it.
And agreement that comes too fast. Ask, what would make this fail?

scenes.headline: End a few minutes early.
scenes.meta: It builds more trust than a perfect agenda.

beats.say: Ending a few minutes early builds more trust than a perfect agenda.
